title: DAL v0 safety and evidence contract
audience: Agents and maintainers changing feedback, policy, evaluation, approval, controller, runtime-generation, or HMR-candidate behavior

claims.text: Campaign replay regrades supplied digest-pinned outputs and recomputes resumable comparison history. It reports proxy and qualification results plus simulated retention, but executes no candidate or model and grants no activation authority. The separate live text path requires an exact campaign grant and native-host mount decision.

Historical version 0 remains local-only by default with independently approved purpose-specific executors and quarantined HMR. The versioned live extension permits bounded native Codex calls; local prompt promotion additionally requires an exact current human candidate decision and separate host-mount approval. Replay-only exploration policy comparison has no activation authority and supplies no arbitrary code evolution or shared-profile authority.
Deterministic schema, privacy, policy, provenance, budget, and quarantine checks may block but cannot authorize a sensitive action.
Shared configuration, plugin management, external transfer, and candidate application require a separate exact, current human approval at the execution boundary.

Live discovery history records parent-linked evaluated nodes under one fixed bounded policy. Dream replay reuses only prefix-revealed stored outcomes, performs no model or evaluator call, and can influence only a later human-approved frozen plan.
A passing offline scorecard is prerequisite evidence only; a hard stop quarantines or requests manual rollback and blocks proposal progression.

The tau-style benchmark separates harness and business outcomes, requires evaluator-owned effect evidence where declared, and permits full model batches only through the approval-bound Docker candidate/service/grader topology.

Controller estimation publishes deterministic observation-only state from one compatible task batch and requires stable, policy-qualified, repository-verified runtime generation evidence in addition to the legacy harness pin; the optional run-mode bridge enrolls only compatible closed terminal records without replacing attestation, and insufficient evidence cannot invoke adaptation or grant authority.

DAL validates RFC 8785 runtime manifests, consumes an optional launcher-owned session binding, and rejects unstable or unverified controller evidence, but current DSH does not yet produce authoritative composition, resolver, artifact, or transition evidence or await final recorder disposal.

The isolated HMR helper can stage and digest a bounded plugin candidate, but application fails before approval verification or any live-file write. Observed hmr/reload events are diagnostic only, no state becomes admitted, drifted rejection never overwrites live files, and promotion remains human-controlled.

retrieval_pointers.when: Changing persisted JSON fields or enum values
Deciding whether evidence, review, or approval may permit an action
Working near shared, external, plugin, or candidate-application behavior
Changing runtime identity, attestation assurance, session binding, or controller generation eligibility

limits: This capsule summarizes reviewed v0 contracts and does not replace schema validation.
It provides no authoritative DSH runtime-generation production, HMR readiness or imported-closure identity, final-disposal durability, OS sandbox, optimizer, model, or external-service proof.
Validate source digests and freshness before using these claims.
